title: All 22 Indian Crew Safe After Tanker MT GEM No.2 Attacked Off UAE Coast
excerpt: The fully laden Panama-flagged tanker was struck at anchor off the UAE on Friday, sparking a fire; New Delhi says it is in direct contact with the ship's managers while seafarers' unions demand stronger protection for Indian crews.
body:
• All 22 Indian crew members aboard the Panama-flagged oil tanker MT GEM No.2 are safe after the vessel was struck in UAE waters on Friday, October 9, the Indian consulate said on Sunday.
  • The fully laden 302,000-tonne vessel was hit by what maritime agencies called an unidentified projectile and India's ports minister called a drone attack, sparking a fire at anchor that was later brought under control.
  • Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal said his ministry is monitoring the situation and is in direct contact with the ship's management company; the UAE Coast Guard separately said it rescued 22 crew from a burning tanker without naming the vessel.
  • Seafarers' unions want a PM-led crisis team for Indian crews in conflict zones, as assaults on commercial shipping in the Gulf and Black Sea multiply.

All 22 Indian crew members aboard the Panama-flagged oil tanker MT GEM No.2 are safe after the vessel was hit in waters off the United Arab Emirates on Friday, the Indian government said, ending a tense two-day wait for the seafarers' families.

The strike hit the fully laden, 302,000-deadweight-tonne crude tanker at anchor and sparked a fire that was later brought under control. The Indian consulate confirmed the crew had been rescued and were safe after the incident off the UAE's Ras Al Khaimah coast, Reuters reported, giving no further details.

Union minister for ports, shipping and waterways Sarbananda Sonowal had said on Friday night that the tanker came under drone attack at Sharjah Anchorage, that all 22 Indian seafarers were "completely safe," and that his ministry was continuously monitoring the situation and in contact with the vessel's management company.

Context & Background

The MT GEM No.2 is a Panama-flagged crude oil tanker of 302,000 deadweight tonnes, managed in Taiwan and linked to U-Ming Marine Transport, according to maritime security firm Vanguard, which named the vessel.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2108755686796788051

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported on Friday that an unidentified projectile had struck a vessel in UAE waters and that the resulting fire had been brought under control. Vanguard said the tanker was hit at around 10 am GMT on Friday, after which it sent a distress message reporting a fire, and vessel-tracking data showed the fully laden tanker anchored off the UAE coast. Two shipping and security sources told Reuters the vessel was the GEM No.2.

A day after the attack, the UAE National Guard said the country's Coast Guard had rescued 22 crew members from a burning oil tanker in Gulf waters. According to the Emirates News Agency, specialist Coast Guard teams located the vessel and brought all 22 crew, described as Asian nationals, to safety in stable condition. The National Guard did not disclose the tanker's name or the cause of the fire, and it is not yet confirmed whether the operation involved the same vessel.

Impact & Analysis

The attack is the latest in a string of assaults on commercial shipping and merchant mariners in the Gulf region and the Black Sea in recent weeks. Responding to the pattern, India and Liberia launched the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers during the 81st United Nations General Assembly; the group held its inaugural meeting in New York with 25 countries taking part, co-chaired by India's external affairs minister S. Jaishankar and Liberia's foreign minister Sara Beysolow Nyanti. The co-chairs issued a joint statement condemning attacks on vessels as indefensible and called for an immediate end to actions disrupting maritime trade.

"We have seen the tweet from the Honourable Minister of Shipping and Ports that MT GEM No.2, with the 22 Indian seafarers, which was anchored at Sharjah, was attacked... And it has been reported that all crew are safe."

— Manoj Yadav, General Secretary, Federation of Seafarers' Unions of India

Federation of Seafarers' Unions of India general secretary Manoj Yadav called for a high-level crisis management team under the Prime Minister to assess threats to Indian seafarers operating in conflict-affected waters, with coordinated involvement from the defence establishment, the Navy and the shipping industry.

Diaspora Angle

The UAE hosts one of the world's largest Indian expatriate communities, and Indian nationals form a significant share of the global seafaring workforce, so the strike on a tanker carrying an all-Indian crew landed close to home for thousands of seafaring families. The first official word of the crew's safety brought visible relief to an industry whose workers transit the Gulf daily.

What's Next

The extent of the damage to the MT GEM No.2 remains unclear, and no authority has yet publicly identified who carried out the attack. The crew's care and any repatriation plans, the formal investigation by UAE authorities, and the question of whether shipping lines reroute Indian-crewed vessels away from threatened waters are the developments to watch in the coming days.
